brief:
Young survivors in Gaza are turning to art as a means of coping with the psychological toll of conflict, according to Al Jazeera English. Drawing, painting, and other creative activities provide these children with safe spaces to express trauma and experience moments of normalcy amid ongoing devastation. Facilitators report that children engage in these programs regularly, finding temporary escape from their circumstances through creative work.

Mental health advocates note that artistic expression allows young survivors to process grief and fear that conventional dialogue may not address. These creative outlets offer glimpses of joy and recovery during a period marked by loss and displacement. Participants have described the experience as restorative, giving them opportunities to rediscover aspects of childhood interrupted by conflict.
dek: Young survivors of Israel's genocidal war in Gaza find safe spaces to process trauma and rediscover joy.
title: Gaza children use art to process war trauma and find refuge
